newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House panel approves oil reserve leasing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House panel approves oil reserve leasing.

text.p: The U.S. House Commerce Committee Wednesday approved budget measures to lease unused space in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to other countries, sell surplus government uranium, and authorize the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to continue collecting industry fees.
The committee quickly approved an administration-backed plan to lease excess space in the SPR to allow other countries to store oil there to generate an estimated $13 million.
After 2002, revenue from leasing would go to buy more oil for the reserve, or to operate and maintain it.
The committee also approved a measure requiring the Energy Department to sell 3.2 million pounds of surplus uranium per year in fiscal years 1999-2000 to generate $150-$175 million.
It narrowly rejected a Democratic amendment to bar the sale if the energy secretary determined it was not in the best interest of the country, particularly if uranium prices were depressed.
Michigan Democrat John Dingell blamed "budgeteers" for forcing the committee to require sales that could lose money for taxpayers if uranium prices plunged.
Dingell said requiring the annual sales, which is necessary to score the sale as upcoming revenue in the budget, could force "a firesale which none of us would want to have our fingerprints on."
But Republicans said the bill had adequate safeguards to ensure a "fair market return" on the uranium sales.

The committee also voted to authorize the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to continue collecting industry fees to fund operations for another four years, over objections from some Democrats who said the committee should have oversight hearings on the agency before reauthorizing it.
Republicans said if the fees were not extended, the committee would have to find $1.4 billion in revenue from another program to meet the budget plan.
